1. Project Overview

sqtseries is a local, single-file time-series database. You feed it measurements — metric + value + optional string tags — and later ask questions like "average CPU over the last hour" or "99th percentile response time this week". Everything lives in one SQLite file (~/.sqtseries/data/db.sqlite by default), so you can copy, back up, or inspect it like any file.

Two transports expose the same JSON wire format:

  • ZeroMQ — PUSH ingest (12501), REP queries (12502), XPUB streaming (12503), REP admin (12504), PUB stats events (12506). High throughput, any language with a ZMQ binding.
  • HTTP — FastAPI REST + WebSocket on 12505. Works from curl, browsers, and any language.

Performance comes from two storage tricks: monthly partitions (measurements_YYYY_MM WITHOUT ROWID tables) and hourly rollups (a background task pre-aggregates completed hours into rollup_hourly so wide queries read a few rows instead of millions). A query fast path merges rollup rows with the raw edges of the window — exact same answer, about 9× faster.

2. Architecture at a Glance

Everything runs in one process: the event loop drives the ZMQ sockets and the HTTP gateway reads the same in-memory engine objects (StorageEngine, TimeSeriesDB, PubSub). There is no service-to-service hop.

            ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
            │                       sqtseries process                   │
  PUSH 12501►│  Ingress (PULL) ─► _sink ─► StorageEngine ─► SQLite (WAL)│
  (write)    │      │                     └──► measurements_YYYY_MM     │
            │      └─► on_publish ─► PubSub (XPUB 12503) ─► SUB clients│
  REQ 12502►│  QueryBroker (REP) ─► TimeSeriesDB ─► store               │
  (query)    │                          │ (rollup fast path + raw edges)│
  REQ 12504►│  AdminBroker (REP) ─► health / stats / backup / vacuum    │
  (admin)    │                          │                               │
  HTTP 12505►│  FastAPI gateway ───► store / tsdb / pubsub / registry   │
  REST + WS │       ├── /ws/subscribe ◄── PubSub (live measurements)    │
            │       └── /ws/connections ◄── ConnectionRegistry          │
  PUB 12506◄│  StatsPublisher (PUB) ◄── ConnectionRegistry (conn/sub)   │
  (events)   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                          │
                          ▼
   db.sqlite (WAL) + runtime.json + backups/ — one directory
   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ series               (metric, tags JSON) → series_id    │
   │ measurements_YYYY_MM WITHOUT ROWID, PK(series_id, ts_ns)│
   │ rollup_hourly        (count, sum, min, max per hour)    │
   │ rollup_meta          (last_hour watermark)              │
   │ schema_version       (migrations)                       │
   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Ingest auto-detection: with ports.auto_detect = true (the default) the ingest port is the first free port in [12500+offset, 12700+offset] that is not one of the fixed ports — so it is usually 12500, not the configured 12501. The active ports are written to runtime.json next to the database; sqtseries ports / sqtseries status read them back.

3. Core Concepts

3.1 Measurement → series → partition

  • A measurement is one number: metric (string), value (finite number), optional tags (string→string map), optional timestamp (epoch seconds; server time when omitted).
  • Internally storage uses nanosecond epoch integers (timestamp_ns); the wire protocol sends seconds, ZMQ queries take nanosecond bounds, and HTTP uses seconds.
  • A series is the unique pair (metric, tags). It gets an integer series_id from the series table (unique index on (metric, tags)). Writing the same (metric, tags) again appends to the same series; different tag sets are different series.
  • Measurements are stored in monthly partitions named measurements_YYYY_MM, created lazily on first write. Partitions are WITHOUT ROWID tables with the clustered primary key (series_id, timestamp_ns) plus a secondary index on timestamp_ns (cross-series time ranges and retention).

3.2 Tags: dimensions, not IDs

Tags are dimensions you slice by: {"host": "web1", "env": "prod"}. Every distinct tag set creates a new series, so never tag high-cardinality values (request IDs, session IDs, timestamps) — they multiply series and slow per-series queries. Tag values must be strings; non-string values are rejected (HTTP 400 / ProtocolError). Wire queries over a metric merge all of its tag sets; per-series breakdowns need the embedded Python API (StorageEngine.series_ids_for_metric + get_series_meta).

3.3 Hourly rollup

  • A background task rolls completed hours into rollup_hourly (series_id, hour_start_ns, count, sum, min, max; avg = sum/count).
  • Only hours that ended at least reject_client_timestamp_skew_s ago are rolled, so a "late" write (a client clock within the skew window) can never land in a rolled hour — kept in-order by the clock-skew guard on ingest.
  • A last_hour watermark in rollup_meta records how far the rollup advanced; each run scans only the data since the previous run, and INSERT OR REPLACE keeps re-runs idempotent.
  • The current (in-progress) hour is always read live from the raw partitions, so results are never stale.

3.4 Query fast path

TimeSeriesDB.query decides whether a query can be answered from the rollup (_rollup_eligible): the aggregation must be expressible from count/sum/min/max (avg, sum, min, max, count), the interval must be a whole-hour multiple (or None), the window must contain at least one fully-inside rolled hour, and the tail must not extend past the watermark. The eligible window is split into three disjoint sources — raw left edge hour, rollup middle hours, raw right tail — merged per bucket, so nothing is counted twice. median, p95, p99, first, last always take the raw path.

3.5 Retention

Retention drops whole monthly partitions whose last day falls before now − ttl (fast DROP TABLE), and deletes those hours from rollup_hourly so deleted data leaves no aggregate trace. TTL syntax: 30d, 12h, 4w, 90s, 45m.

3.6 Crash safety

  • SQLite WAL journal: every write is a single atomic transaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE).
  • Startup: PRAGMA quick_check, then recover_wal (re-assert WAL mode + a PASSIVE checkpoint). A failed integrity check logs the problems; strict mode raises.
  • Shutdown: PRAGMA optimize, then a TRUNCATE checkpoint so the next start is fast.
  • Backups use VACUUM INTO — a consistent snapshot even while writes are in flight.

3.7 Configuration precedence

Defaults < config file (TOML/YAML/JSON, SQT_SERIES_CONFIG_FILE or --config) < environment variables (SQT_SERIES_<SECTION>__<KEY>, e.g. SQT_SERIES_DATABASE__PATH). Env always wins over file values — the loader computes the set of env-set leaf paths and only merges file keys the env did not set.

config.tomlannotated configuration sample

Every configurable section with defaults and comments (see Configuration for the full table and precedence rules). Pass with --config config.toml to any command, or set SQT_SERIES_CONFIG_FILE. Environment variables (SQT_SERIES_*) override file values. The file is optional — the service starts with built-in defaults out of the box.

src/sqtseries/client.py262 lines

High-level Python client for a running service. Wraps the ZeroMQ transports: PUSH (write, 12501), REQ (query, 12502), SUB (subscribe, 12503), REQ (admin, 12504). Uses the same JSON wire format as the HTTP gateway.

Module constants

DEFAULT_HOST = "127.0.0.1"
DEFAULT_PORTS = {"write": 12501, "query": 12502, "subscribe": 12503, "admin": 12504}
RECV_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000 — query/admin replies time out to ClientError instead of hanging.
WRITE_LINGER_MS = 2000 — the write PUSH socket flushes queued measurements for 2 s on close; zero would drop a measurement written immediately before exit.

Class Client

Usage: Client(), client.write("cpu.usage", 0.72, {"host": "web1"}), client.query("cpu.usage", start=..., end=...) (nanoseconds), iterate client.subscribe("cpu."). Supports the context manager protocol.

method
__init__(self, host="127.0.0.1", ports: dict | None = None)

Stores host/port map (merging over DEFAULT_PORTS) and lazily opens sockets via the _get_*_sock helpers. All four sockets are created on demand from one zmq.Context().

method
write(metric, value, tags=None, timestamp=None) -> None

Send one measurement (PUSH, fire-and-forget). Optional timestamp is epoch seconds. Serialized with orjson.

method
write_many(points: list[dict]) -> None

Send multiple raw point dicts, one frame each (a convenience loop, not a server-side batch).

method
query(metric, start=None, end=None, *, aggregation=None, interval=None, limit=None, order="asc") -> list[dict]

Run a query and return [{timestamp, value}, ...] with timestamps in seconds (the server converts ns → s). start/end are epoch nanoseconds. On a recv timeout it replaces the broken REQ socket (REQ enforces strict send/recv alternation — a timed-out recv leaves the socket unusable, so _reset_sock closes it and the next call recreates it) and raises ClientError("query timed out...").

method
aggregate(metric, start=None, end=None, *, funcs=None) -> dict[str, float]

Compute one or more aggregations over a window; returns {func: value}. Sends {"type": "query", "metric": ..., "aggregations": "avg,min,..."}.

method
admin(cmd, **kwargs) -> dict

Send an admin command to port 12504: ping / health / stats / optimize / backup / vacuum / connections / conncheck / subscribers. Extra kwargs become part of the request, e.g. admin("conncheck", ids=["abc"]). Error replies raise ClientError.

method
subscribe(topic="*", timeout=0.5) -> Iterator[dict | None]

Yield live measurement dicts matching topic (SUB socket). Polls with a timeout and yields None as a heartbeat when idle, so callers can break out of the loop cleanly. Frames are [topic, payload]; yields the parsed payload. The poll-then- recv_multipart(NOBLOCK) pattern is per pyzmq docs (avoids blocking recv vs context close).

method
_get_write_sock/_get_query_sock/_get_sub_sock/_get_admin_sock() -> zmq.Socket

Lazy socket factories. Write: PUSH, SNDHWM 10000, LINGER 2000. Query/Admin: REQ, LINGER 500, RCVTIMEO 30 s. Subscribe: SUB, LINGER 0.

method
_reset_sock(attr)

Close a broken socket so the next call recreates it. Only REQ sockets strictly need this (strict alternation after a recv timeout); harmless for the others.

method
close()

Close all sockets and terminate the context (idempotent). The write socket keeps its flush linger so queued-but-undelivered measurements are still sent.

method
__enter__ / __exit__

Context-manager support; exit calls close().

Class ClientError(Exception)

Raised when the service returns an error reply, or a query/admin call times out.

Commands

command
run

Start the service in the foreground. Guards: refuses to start when the runtime file says another live sqtseries process already serves the same database (or a different one is being served — a conflict). Prints a note if other *.sqlite files sit in the same directory. Configures logging, builds Service(settings), and runs start → run → shutdown under asyncio.run, suppressing KeyboardInterrupt (clean SIGINT shutdown path).

command
stop

Send SIGTERM to the pid in runtime.json (validated: must be a live sqtseries process, and the runtime's db_path must match what this invocation resolves — refuses to stop the wrong instance). Then waits up to 10 s for the runtime file to disappear (clean shutdown removes it last) or the pid to vanish, so a restart script cannot race a still-dying process.

command
status

Show running/not-running, version, database path, and every active port from runtime.json; warns when the config resolves to a different database than the running instance.

command
ports

Show active ports from runtime.json, or the configured ports when not running.

command
health

Open the database read-only and run quick_check; exit code 0 = ok, 1 = degraded.

command
stats

Open the database and print metric and series counts (StorageEngine.list_metrics, series_count).

command
vacuum

Full VACUUM — requires the service to be stopped (VACUUM can't run inside a transaction / under active connections).

command
optimize

PRAGMA optimize — refresh query-planner statistics.

command
backup

backup_database(engine, settings.backup.path) — consistent VACUUM INTO snapshot; prints the written path.

command
install [--system]

Install the systemd unit (user-level by default; --system needs root). Embeds the current interpreter and --config if one was passed, plus db path and backup path.

command
uninstall [--system]

Disable and remove the systemd unit.

class
Settings(BaseSettings)

Top-level settings. Env prefix SQT_SERIES_, nested delimiter __, env_ignore_empty=True (VAR= means "unset"), case-insensitive. Holds every section above plus config_file. Key methods:

  • load(config_file=None) -> Settings — precedence: defaults < file < env < init kwargs. Implementation detail: pydantic-settings gives init kwargs priority over env, so the loader instantiates twice — first with env applied, then re-instantiates with only the file leaf paths that the environment did not set.
  • db_path_expanded() -> str — database path with ~ expanded.

Module functions

function
_enviro_leaf_paths() -> set[tuple[str, ...]]

Scans os.environ for SQT_SERIES_* keys, converts SQT_SERIES_DATABASE__BATCH_SIZE → ("database", "batch_size"), normalizes case, excludes the root CONFIG_FILE key.

function
_iter_leaf_paths(mapping, prefix=())

Yield (path, value) for every leaf of a nested mapping (recursive).

function

Set target[path] = value, creating intermediate dicts.

function
_read_config_file(path) -> dict

TOML (tomllib), YAML (requires pyyaml, else a clear ValueError), or JSON (orjson); any other suffix raises. JSON/YAML must be a top-level mapping.

function
validate_settings(settings) -> list[str]

Returns a list of configuration errors (empty when valid): ports in 1–65535 and unique, hwm/pending_max/batch_size ≥ 1, batch_size ≤ 8191 (SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER safety), max_websocket_connections ≥ 1, and duration strings parse correctly (rollup.interval, maintenance.analyze_interval, retention TTLs, backup.interval) — each validated only when its feature is enabled.

src/sqtseries/logging.py78 lines

Structured logging via structlog over stdlib logging: JSON output for production, pretty console for development, optional rotating file output.

function
_json_serializer(obj, **_) -> str

orjson-backed serializer for the JSON renderer.

function
configure_logging(settings: LoggingSettings) -> BoundLogger

Builds the processor chain: contextvars merge → add_log_level → ISO UTC timestamps → StackInfoRenderer → format_exc_info (plain strings so both renderers can display tracebacks) → JSONRenderer or ConsoleRenderer (colors when stderr is a tty). Configures the stdlib root logger, adds a 10 MB / 5-backup RotatingFileHandler when settings.file is set (skips if a handler for that file already exists — avoids duplicates on repeated calls), then calls structlog.configure and returns structlog.get_logger("sqtseries").

method
async start()

Calls _start(); on any failure runs shutdown() to clean up whatever started, then re-raises.

method
async _start()

The boot sequence, in order:

  1. Open the engine (create_sqlite_engine), run migrations, check integrity (non-strict), recover WAL.
  2. Build StorageEngine + TimeSeriesDB.
  3. Start each enabled background manager (checkpoint, rollup with the skew window, maintenance, retention, backup).
  4. Start PubSub (XPUB) wired to the connection registry.
  5. Allocate the ingest port via PortAllocator — with auto_detect, it must avoid the five fixed ports (stats included), then start Ingress with _sink and _on_publish callbacks.
  6. Start the query broker (REP) and admin broker (REP, no handler timeout — admin ops such as backup/vacuum may run long).
  7. Start the WorkerPool (size 1) whose step pumps all three ZMQ sockets with block=False and reports whether any had work (the worker then sleeps 0 vs 10 ms — avoids GIL starvation of CPU-bound threads).
  8. Start the stats publisher (if enabled), then the HTTP gateway.
  9. Run ANALYZE once (only after every socket bound, so failed boots in a restart loop don't hammer planner stats).
  10. Write runtime.json with the real ports; set _runtime_owned = True.

method
async _start_http_gateway()

Builds the FastAPI app via create_app, runs uvicorn's Server.serve() as an asyncio task sharing the loop, and waits up to 5 s for started. uvicorn is configured with log_config=None/access_log=False (structlog owns logging), timeout_graceful_shutdown=5, ws_max_size=16 MiB, ws_ping_interval=20, ws_ping_timeout=20. Note: uvicorn 0.52 installs its own signal handlers, but Service.run()'s add_signal_handler replaces them, so should_exit is only ever set in shutdown(). Bind failure surfaces a clean RuntimeError.

method
_sink(metric, tags, value, ts_ns)

Persist one ingested measurement immediately via store.insert_many. There is no app-level write queue: SQLite serializes writers itself (single-writer + BEGIN IMMEDIATE + busy_timeout), so a queue would only add latency.

method
_on_publish(topic, payload)

Fire an asyncio task per measurement to republish to live subscribers; tasks are tracked in _publish_tasks and drained on shutdown.

Serves the query REP socket: validates limit, dispatches the aggregations (comma-separated) form to ts.aggregate, otherwise to ts.query, converts ns → seconds timestamps, and maps value/type errors to INVALID_QUERY.

method
_admin_handler(query) -> dict

Serves admin commands: ping, health, stats, optimize, backup, vacuum (VACUUM_BUSY error shape when it fails while running — recommends sqtseries vacuum stopped), connections, conncheck, subscribers. Unknown commands raise ProtocolError → INVALID_REQUEST reply.

method

Assembles live counters from every component: ingested/invalid/ingest_errors, queries, admin_requests, wal_bytes/checkpoint_busy_runs/checkpoints, analyze_runs, retention_runs/partitions_dropped, backup_runs/backups_created/last_backup, published/subscribers, series/metrics, uptime_s.

method

Delegates to the ConnectionRegistry: active WebSocket list; which of the given IDs are present; per-topic ZMQ subscriber counts.

method

Wraps collect_health(self.engine, started_at=...).

method
async run()

Waits for SIGINT/SIGTERM using an asyncio.Event (not loop.stop() — stopping the loop mid-run makes asyncio.run raise, which systemd's Restart=on-failure would treat as a crash). Falls back to signal.signal when add_signal_handler is unavailable (non-main thread).

method
async shutdown()

Graceful shutdown, in dependency order: stop background managers, the worker pool, the three ZMQ sockets, ask uvicorn to exit (should_exit = True), drain in-flight publishes before stopping pubsub, stop pubsub and stats publisher, close the store, run optimize + TRUNCATE checkpoint on the engine, dispose it, and remove runtime.json only if this instance wrote it (a failed second start must not delete a healthy instance's state).

6. Package sqtseries.engine

The raw sqlite3 storage layer: schema, partitions, PRAGMAs, migrations, checkpoints, backups, maintenance. Why raw sqlite3 (per the module docs): benchmark-validated 2026-08-07 — roughly 6.7× faster point lookups and 1.2× bulk inserts than alternatives on the exact hot paths; aiosqlite rejected (sequential thread hops).

src/sqtseries/engine/__init__.py40 lines

Re-exports the public engine API: BackupExistsError, BackupManager, CheckpointManager, Connection, Database, MaintenanceManager, SeriesNotFoundError, StorageEngine, backup_database, backup_latest, create_sqlite_engine, get_schema_version, incremental_vacuum, initialize_schema, integrity_check, quick_check, run_analyze_once, run_migrations, run_optimize, upgrade, wal_checkpoint.

src/sqtseries/engine/db.py248 lines

The raw sqlite3 layer. Reader/writer split: connect() gives a read-only connection that never checkpoints the WAL; begin() gives a writer transaction using BEGIN IMMEDIATE (takes the write lock up front — under WAL a deferred read→write upgrade returns SQLITE_BUSY immediately, which busy_timeout cannot retry).

Module constants

CONNECTION_PRAGMAS — applied to every new connection: journal_mode WAL, synchronous NORMAL, cache_size -64000, mmap_size 256 MiB, busy_timeout 5000, temp_store MEMORY, foreign_keys ON, locking_mode NORMAL, journal_size_limit 64 MiB, threads 4, analysis_limit 400.
READER_AUTOCHECKPOINT = 0 / WRITER_AUTOCHECKPOINT = 10000 — readers never trigger checkpoints (prevents reader-writer contention); the writer checkpoints every ~80 MB at 8192-byte pages (10× fewer fsync spikes than the default 1000 pages).

Class Result

Thin wrapper over sqlite3.Cursor. __slots__ for memory. Methods: fetchall(), fetchone(), first(), scalar() (first column of first row), properties lastrowid / rowcount, __getitem__(idx) (fetchone + IndexError), __iter__ (iterates rows).

Class Connection

Wraps a raw connection; context manager commits on clean exit and always closes. execute(sql, params) / exec_driver_sql / executescript / executemany all return a Result; dbapi_connection property exposes the raw object; commit()/rollback()/close() delegate. Cursors are closed on sqlite3.Error before re-raising.

Fresh READER connection (autocheckpoint 0, transaction=False).

contextmanager

src/sqtseries/partition/rollup.py280 lines

Rollup pre-aggregation: store per-series per-hour (count, sum, min, max) in rollup_hourly; average is derived as sum/count. Only completed hours are rolled; the current hour is always served from raw partitions. The last_hour watermark in rollup_meta records progress; INSERT OR REPLACE keeps re-runs idempotent. Documented assumption: in-order ingestion for completed hours — a write backfilled into an already-rolled past hour is not picked up until a rebuild with replace=True.

ROLLUP_TABLE = "rollup_hourly" / ROLLUP_META = "rollup_meta" / META_LAST_HOUR = "last_hour"

class

Wraps a StorageEngine. Methods:

  • insert(metric, value, tags=None, timestamp_ns=None) -> int — single measurement; server time when no timestamp.
  • query(metric=None, series_ids=None, start=None, end=None, *, aggregation=None, interval=None, limit=None, order="asc", fill_gaps_ns=None) -> list[(ts_ns, value)] — the main entry. If eligible (_rollup_eligible) serves from the rollup; otherwise fetches raw and applies: downsample (aggregation+interval), whole-window aggregate anchored at the oldest sample in the window (matching the rollup path's first_sample_ts), or gap-fill. limit keeps the first N in the selected order.

  • aggregate(metric, start, end, *, funcs=None) -> dict[str, float] — per-function whole-window aggregates; each eligible func uses the rollup, and the raw row set is fetched at most once for the others.
  • downsample(metric, start, end, *, interval="5m", aggregation="avg") — sugar over query.
  • _rollup_eligible(...) -> bool — requires: aggregation in ROLLUP_FUNCS; an interval that is None or a whole-hour multiple; watermark > 0; the window's end hour ≤ watermark; at least one fully-inside hour (span ≥ 2 hours) — otherwise raw is faster; and the start not already past the watermark.

class
Ingress

(endpoint, settings, sink=None, on_publish=None, context=None). sink(metric, tags, value, ts_ns) is called synchronously per frame (None skips persistence — validation and republish still happen); on_publish(bytes_metric, dict) feeds live subscribers. Counters: recv_count, error_count, invalid_count.

  • async start() — PULL socket with HWM + max message size, bound to the endpoint.

  • async drain() — drain ALL pending frames in a tight loop (shutdown/tests).
  • _handle(raw) — parse (invalid JSON counts), parse_ingest with the skew guard (ProtocolError/OverflowError → invalid counter — OverflowError guards the huge-float timestamp path where ts * 1e9 can't fit an int), then sink + on_publish.
  • async stop() — close the socket (linger 0).
  • stats() — {recv, invalid, errors}.

Query broker: REP (or ROUTER) socket serving query/aggregate requests with a pluggable handler and an optional handler timeout.

class
QueryBroker

(endpoint, settings, handler=None, context=None, use_router=False, handler_timeout_s=None). Counters requests, errors.

  • async run_once(block=True) -> bool — one request: router multipart or plain frame; returns whether handled.
  • _handle(raw) / _handle_router(frames) — parse (ProtocolError → INVALID_REQUEST), dispatch, and reply; TimeoutError → QUERY_TIMEOUT; any other exception → INTERNAL_ERROR (logged). Replies on REP are sent blocking — a REP socket requires strict recv/send alternation, so dropping a reply on EAGAIN would wedge the broker for every client; router replies use NOBLOCK with a warning on would-block.
  • async _dispatch(query) — with handler_timeout_s the blocking handler runs off the loop in a thread under asyncio.wait_for (a slow query never stalls the event loop; over budget → QUERY_TIMEOUT). None/≤0 runs synchronously inline.

class

(endpoint, *, linger_seconds=30.0, hwm=10000, context=None, registry=None).

src/sqtseries/messaging/connection_registry.py190 lines

Connection and subscription registry: tracks every active WebSocket connection and ZMQ SUB subscriber so the service can answer connections, conncheck, and subscribers queries at any time. Events carry arrival/leaving timestamps (connected_at/left_at for WS; arrived_at/left_at plus first_seen for ZMQ topics).

class
ConnectionRegistry

Internal maps: _ws (conn_id → entry), _zmq_subs (topic → count), _zmq_first_seen, _listeners. Stale-connection detection is read-only (see sweep_stale below). Methods:

  • on_event(callback) / remove_listener(callback) — subscribe/unsubscribe to (event_type, payload) pairs ("conn", "sub"). remove_listener must be paired with every on_event or repeated start/stop cycles grow listeners without bound.
  • register_ws(conn_id, peer, topic) — record a WS join; emit a "conn" event (connected: True, ttl 60). Sets connected_at and last_activity_at.
  • unregister_ws(conn_id) — mark gone; the leave event carries connected_at and left_at for duration display.
  • touch_ws(conn_id) — update last_activity_at on every received frame (keepalive ping, client message, etc.). Called from the websocket handler on every inbound frame and keepalive.
  • sweep_stale(expired_timeout_s=30.0, batch_size=None) -> list[dict] — return connections whose last_activity_at is older than the deadline, oldest-idle first. Entries include age_s for diagnostics. batch_size caps the result so callers can pace eviction across ticks. Does NOT remove connections (caller decides).
  • register_zmq_sub(topic) / unregister_zmq_sub(topic) — increment/decrement per-topic counts, emit "sub" events; first_seen set when a topic goes 0 → 1 (ttl 30 on joins).
  • check_connection(conn_id) -> bool — conncheck support.
  • list_connections() -> list[dict] — sorted by connected_at.
  • subscriber_count(topic=None) -> int, active_topics(), properties ws_count / zmq_sub_count.
  • snapshot() -> dict — read-only summary: ws_connections, zmq_subscribers, active_topics, connections list, per-topic subscriptions with first_seen (used by /ws/connections, admin subscribers, and the stats report).

src/sqtseries/messaging/worker.py74 lines

Worker pool: N asyncio workers consuming from ingress and serving queries. ZMQ sockets are not thread-shared; asyncio tasks on the same socket are safe only via the single event loop — so the pool lives on one loop with cooperative workers. (For multiple processes: ProcessPool + per-process context.)

class
WorkerPool

(step, *, size=1) where step() is an async callable doing one unit of work and returning True if it did any. async start() spawns size tasks; each worker loop calls step, sleeps 0 ms when work flowed, 10 ms when idle — a NOBLOCK recv raising zmq.Again does NOT release the event loop, so a tight idle loop would starve timers and CPU-bound threads (verified: 112k spins/sec starved call_later; 10 ms only delays the first message after idle, and busy cycles use sleep(0) with no added latency). async stop() cancels and awaits all; property running.

10. Package sqtseries.gateway

HTTP gateway (FastAPI REST + WebSocket) on port 12505. Bridges HTTP directly to the engine — single-process architecture, no ZMQ hop.

src/sqtseries/gateway/__init__.py6 lines

Exports create_app and router.

src/sqtseries/gateway/app.py218 lines

REST + WebSocket gateway factory with CORS, rate limiting, request-ID and security-header middleware.

function
create_app(store=None, tsdb=None, settings=None, pubsub=None, ingestion=None, registry=None, query_timeout_s=None) -> FastAPI

Builds the app. tsdb is created from store when absent. Everything shared lives on app.state: tsdb, store, pubsub, settings, ingestion (skew guard for HTTP writes), registry, query_timeout_s, ws_count/ws_max_connections (live WebSocket budget). Middleware (LIFO — last added runs outermost): request-ID middleware (outermost; echoes or generates an X-Request-ID), security headers middleware (CSP default-src 'self', X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, X-XSS-Protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy), rate limiter, then CORS nearest the router. CORS and the rate limiter short-circuit non-HTTP scopes, so WebSockets bypass both. Endpoints:

  • GET /api/v1/health — {"status": ok|degraded, "version"} via is_ready.
  • WS /ws/subscribe?metric=* — accept; enforce the 1000-connection cap (close 1013 "too many connections"); delegate to subscribe_and_forward; close 1008 when streaming is disabled; decrement the slot in finally.
  • WS /ws/connections — push-only live connection/subscription feed: sends a snapshot on connect, then one frame per registry change. Registry callbacks may fire from any thread, so events are marshalled onto the loop via call_soon_threadsafe into a bounded queue (backlog > 500 drops the oldest — a stalled client must not grow memory unbounded), drained by a sender task paired with a disconnect watcher.

function
_ws_slot_available(app) -> bool

Check-and-increment of the WebSocket cap. Single-threaded event loop: no await between check and increment, so concurrent handlers cannot overshoot the cap.

src/sqtseries/gateway/routes.py292 lines

REST routes, all under /api/v1. Times on the wire are epoch seconds; the engine uses ns internally.

_WRITE_BODY = Body(...) — module-level sentinel for FastAPI body binding; _DEFAULT_QUERY_TIMEOUT_S = 30.0.
POST
/api/v1/write

Ingest one object or an array of rows. Batch semantics: validate the WHOLE batch first (a bad item rejects the batch — retry-safe, nothing partially persists), persist in ONE transaction (_insert_validated_batch; timestamp-less rows get distinct ns values so two same-series rows can't collide on the clustered PK), then republish to live subscribers (_broadcast — best-effort; a failing broadcast must not turn a successful write into a 500). Returns {"status": "ok", "written": n}. Validation mirrors the ZMQ path: non-empty metric, finite number, string→string tags, numeric timestamp within int64 ns and within the clock skew guard.

GET
/api/v1/read?metric=&start=&end=&aggregation=&interval=&limit=&order=

Query rows; returns {"status": "ok", "data": [{timestamp (s), value}]}. limit ge=1 le=100000, order pattern ^(asc|desc)$. Runs off the event loop in a thread under query_timeout_s (504 GATEWAY_TIMEOUT on expiry).

GET
/api/v1/aggregate?metric=&start=&end=&funcs=

Comma-separated funcs (default "avg") over a window; returns {"status": "ok", "aggregations": {func: value}}.

GET
/api/v1/stats

{"status": "ok", "metrics": n, "series": n} from the store.

GET
/api/v1/connections

Live WebSocket connection list from the registry (kind/peer/topic/connected_at).

GET
/api/v1/subscribers

Live ZMQ subscriptions: {"status": "ok", "zmq_subscribers": n, "subscriptions": [...]}.

Seconds → ns; overflow raises 400.

Full per-row validation with HTTPException(400) details; rejects timestamps outside int64 ns and beyond the skew guard.

Best-effort republish of HTTP writes.

_insert_validated / _insert_validated_batch

Single-row insert / one-transaction batch insert with distinct server ns for timestamp-less rows.

function
async _run_query(request, fn)

Run a blocking query off the loop (asyncio.to_thread + wait_for, timeout from query.timeout_s) so a slow aggregate can't stall WS streaming or admin; abandoned threads finish in the background and their results are discarded.

src/sqtseries/gateway/ratelimit.py63 lines

Fixed-window rate limiting middleware.

class
RateLimitMiddleware

ASGI middleware rejecting requests over limit_per_minute per fixed 60 s window, keyed by the client peer address. The X-Forwarded-For header is deliberately NOT trusted (client-controlled; anyone could rotate it to bypass). Memory-bounded: keys from other windows are swept when the table exceeds 10 000 entries, and excess current-window keys are evicted FIFO. Over-limit replies with the standard error shape and HTTP 429.

src/sqtseries/gateway/websocket.py115 lines

WebSocket subscription handler — proxies live measurements from the pubsub XPUB socket to the WS client and tracks connection state in the registry. The browser dashboard opens ws://host:12505/ws/subscribe?metric=... and receives every published measurement.

SEND_TIMEOUT = 30.0 — a frame that can't be flushed within 30 s means the client is dead; close it (1011 slow consumer) instead of holding the connection and its ZMQ subscription hostage.
function
async subscribe_and_forward(websocket, *, pubsub, topic="*", registry=None)

Creates a conn_id and registers the WS (peer host:port, topic). Opens a SUB socket and subscribes before connect (the subscription then travels with the handshake; subscribing after connect leaves a race where a measurement published in between is dropped). Two sibling tasks: send_loop (recv_multipart with a 30 s wait_for timeout; on timeout sends a {"type":"ping"} keepalive; filters by topic prefix; decodes payload with errors="replace") and watch_disconnect (consumes inbound frames so a client disconnect surfaces immediately instead of lingering until the next send — which would hold uvicorn's graceful shutdown). First task to finish kills the other; the registry entry is always unregistered in finally and the socket closed.

function
async _send(websocket, text, what) -> bool

send_text under SEND_TIMEOUT; on timeout logs, closes 1011, returns False so the caller aborts the stream.

Standalone runnable scripts for every operation. None of them import sqtseries internals (the Client is used where convenient) — the wire-protocol ones replicate what any language can do. Running them requires a live sqtseries run service on the default ports (except run_custom.py which starts its own).

Builds a PUSH socket (SNDHWM 10000, LINGER 500), picks random metric/host from small pools, and sends one JSON frame per point. Every batch points it prints throughput. Closes the socket with linger=2000 so queued points flush instead of being dropped (fire-and-forget PUSH loses everything with linger 0).

  • Questions: q1_busiest_host (per-series avg → ranking), q2_p95_per_page, q3_visitors_per_page, q4_throughput (count/60 per minute), q5_percentile_ladder (median/p95/p99), q6_compare_days (today vs yesterday vs a week ago), q7_busiest_hour (sum & 1h buckets → max), q8_data_quality (expected vs received readings today), q9_trend (day-over-day count slope), q10_staleness.

12. Camera Analytics Stack (examples/camera)

A complete self-contained demo: a simulated camera with edge analytics streams JSON over a WebSocket; camera_feed.py pumps every reading into sqtseries over plain HTTP (no sqtseries import needed — works from any Python environment); camera_feed.py --ask answers 17 questions about the accumulated data; overlay.html is a live dashboard that also subscribes to sqtseries and to the connection feed; sqtcam.sh starts everything in a tmux session.

examples/camera/overlay_server.py237 lines

Overlay HTTP server + WebSocket data generator (FastAPI + uvicorn). Serves overlay.html on HTTP and simulated analytics on /ws/metrics — every 0.25 s by default. Used by OBS browser sources (hence 0.0.0.0 and the S104 ruff ignore).

  • CONFIG — host from TEST_HOST, port from --port/TEST_PORT/ random, push_interval 0.25, error_interval 0 (simulated errors off), camera_id test_cam_001.
  • free_port() — OS-assigned free port.
  • class DataSimulator — stateful random generator: visible people/cars (random-walk around bases), monotonic totals, per-minute rates, battery percent drifting down, battery/cpu temperature, cpu usage; every message carries generated_at (ISO-8601 UTC) and system_metrics. should_error() optionally injects an error payload every error_interval seconds.
  • class ConnectionManager — accept/track/broadcast WebSockets; on broadcast, dead sockets are detected via return_exceptions and disconnected.
  • Routes: GET /overlay.html and GET / serve the dashboard (single self-contained file by design — a trusted, developer-owned artifact for LAN/OBS use; the real API surface, the sqtseries gateway, sends strict security headers); WS /ws/metrics — broadcast a payload every push_interval using wait_for(receive_text, timeout) as the pacing timer.
  • main(argv) — resolves the port and runs uvicorn with ws_max_size 1 MiB, ws_ping 25/10.
examples/camera/camera_feed.py693 lines — the biggest example

Two parts: Pump (default) subscribes to a metrics WebSocket and writes every reading to sqtseries via HTTP; Ask (--ask) answers 17 questions from the stored data. Only needs stdlib + websockets (pump mode) — never imports sqtseries.

Flattening (the core concept)

Each camera message is flattened into flat metric + value + tags measurements tagged with camera_id. 10 numeric fields (FIELD_PATHS, dotted JSON paths like system_metrics.batteryPercent) plus 1 boolean (BOOL_PATHS: detection_overlay_enabled → 1.0/0.0). String fields (batteryHealth, footer, overlay URLs) can't be stored as numbers and are skipped.

  • agg(base, metric, funcs, start_s, end_s) — /api/v1/aggregate helper.
  • series(base, metric, start_s, end_s, interval, func) — /api/v1/read with downsampling; returns [(bucket_ts_s, value)].
  • latest(base, metric, start_s) — newest reading (limit=1, desc).
  • flatten(msg) -> list[dict] — one WebSocket message → write points; uses the message's generated_at as the timestamp (_source_ts), falls back to server time.
  • post_batch(base_url, points) — POST the array; prints HTTP errors (0 for unreachable).
  • The 17 questions: q_traffic_current (averages & extremes), q_busiest_hour_day, q_footfall_total, q_trend (day-over-day), q_turnover (total vs visible), q_percentiles (capacity planning), q_anomaly (current hour vs same hour previous days: mean + 2σ threshold), q_battery (drain rate and projected time-to-empty), q_cpu (usage/temperature profile + >70 °C warning), q_correlation (Pearson r footfall vs CPU per hour), q_battery_vs_busy, q_staleness, q_uptime (received vs expected readings, ~4/s), q_multicam (notes the wire API can't split per-camera — points to --db), q_monthly_projection, q_storage (points/day → MB/day at ~100 B/pt), q_overlay (enabled % of time).
  • ask(base, hours) — runs ALL_QUESTIONS over [now - hours, now], each guarded by try/except so one bad metric can't kill the catalog.
  • main() — --ws URL, --host/--http-port, --ask, --hours, --once (pump one message and exit, for tests). Pump mode: subscribe → flatten → post each message.
examples/camera/overlay.html821 lines — single-file dashboard

The live camera dashboard: a single self-contained HTML page (inline CSS + JS, GitHub-dark theme) meant for OBS browser sources. It connects to /ws/metrics for camera telemetry and — when opened with ?sqtseries=ws://<host>:<port>/ws/subscribe — also subscribes to sqtseries itself and to the /ws/connections feed, so the dashboard doubles as a demonstration of the time-series database's live path.

Layout

Header (camera id, connection-state badge with animated dot, last-updated), an error banner for simulated feed errors, and cards: People (visible now hero, detected total, per minute), Vehicles, Battery (charge hero, temperature, health), CPU (usage hero, temperature, last-reading age), Detection overlay (status, stream URL, footer), and a large Time-series DB card: connection badge, frame counter, live connected-clients table, ZMQ subscribers table, and an activity log. A collapsible raw-last-message viewer and a footer complete the page.

JavaScript behavior

  • render(msg) — updates every metric from one camera message; refreshAge() re-renders the "last reading" age every second.
  • connect() — camera WS with exponential backoff reconnect (1→10 s cap); error payloads → banner.
  • connectDb() — sqtseries WS subscription; records the latest value per metric|camera_id key into a 15-entry Map; ignores {"type":"ping"} keepalives; renders the db table with per-entry age.
  • connectConnWs() — /ws/connections feed: applies the initial snapshot and then conn/sub events (applyConnEvent / applySubEvent) to two Maps; renderClients() renders both tables; activity lines are appended (bounded to 60).
  • Security posture: inline CSS/JS is intentional for this trusted developer-owned artifact (no user input, no third-party content); the sqtseries gateway itself sends strict headers.
examples/camera/conn_validate.py238 lines

Validates the live connection/subscription feed of a running sqtseries. Connects N WebSocket subscribers and M ZMQ SUB subscribers, watches the push-only /ws/connections feed, and asserts every join and leave arrives instantly with the exact figures. Exits non-zero on any mismatch. This backs the camera dashboard's "Connected clients" / "ZMQ subscribers" tables.

  • next_msg(ws, timeout) — one JSON frame with a timeout.
  • wait_for(ws, pred, timeout, label) — consume frames until pred; AssertionError with everything seen on timeout.
  • validate(args) — the full scenario:
    1. Connect to /ws/connections; record the baseline snapshot (ids, per-topic zmq counts).
    2. Join --clients WebSocket subscribers on distinct topics (v0....) — assert a matching conn event within timeout, with connected_at.
    3. Join --zmq-subs ZMQ subscribers on distinct topics (cpu0....) — assert sub events with arrived_at, and exact per-topic counts.
    4. Cross-check via HTTP /api/v1/connections and /api/v1/subscribers — exact figures beyond the baseline.
    5. Leave WS clients one at a time (reverse order) — assert leave events with connected_at ≤ left_at.
    6. Leave ZMQ subscribers — assert counts return to 0, with left_at ≥ first_seen.
    7. Final HTTP check: back to the baseline exactly.
  • parse_args / main(argv) — CLI with --clients (3), --zmq-subs (2), --timeout (5 s).
examples/camera/sqtcam.sh101 lines

One command to run the whole demo: starts sqtseries, the overlay simulator, and the camera feed in a tmux session (sqtcam) so data can collect overnight.

  • Uses a dedicated work dir /tmp/sqtcam with its own config (ports 17101–17106, auto_detect off) — never touches the default service.
  • Prefers the project venv python (~/.env/sqtseries/bin/python3), falls back to python3.
  • Window 1: python3 -m sqtseries --config conf.toml run. Window 2: the overlay server, logging to overlay.log. It then greps the log for the overlay's reported WebSocket port and starts window 3: camera_feed.py --ws ws://localhost:PORT/ws/metrics --http-port 17105.
  • Re-running prints attach instructions instead of duplicating the session.

13. scripts/benchmark.py

scripts/benchmark.py182 lines

Reproducible performance benchmark: SQLite insert throughput + query latency, measuring the raw engine and the rollup fast path. Data is written at evenly spaced intervals over --span-hours across --series series, ending on a completed hour boundary two hours in the past so every measurement is rollable.

  • _completed_hour_end() — start of a completed hour two hours back.
  • _data_bounds(engine) — global MIN/MAX timestamp across partitions.
  • bench_inserts(db_path, rows, batch, series, span_hours) -> dict — inserts rows in batches via store.insert_many, tags {host, id}; returns rows/seconds/rows_per_sec.
  • run_queries(db_path, n) -> dict — measures p50/p95 latencies for: (1) raw single-series 1 h range (clustered PK path); (2) the wide-window avg/1h query before rollup (raw path); (3) the same query after rollup_new_hours — and reports the speedup ratio.
  • main() — --db, --rows (200k), --batch (5000), --series (1000), --span-hours (24), --queries (100).

14. Tests (54 files + conftest.py)

The suite is self-contained: every test uses a temp database under tmp_path — no pre-existing data or running service required. Service-spawning tests use OS-assigned free ports (free_port()), so nothing clashes with a local instance. asyncio_mode = "auto" awaits async tests without markers; a 60 s pytest-timeout guards hangs. Run: python3 -m pytest tests/ -q.

16. Wire Protocol Reference

Both transports carry the same JSON shapes. Timestamps: seconds on the wire (ingest/HTTP and returned rows); ZMQ query bounds are nanoseconds; HTTP query bounds are seconds.

16.1 Ingest (ZMQ PUSH → 12501, or POST /api/v1/write)

{"metric": "cpu.usage", "value": 0.72, "tags": {"host": "web1"}, "timestamp": 1691234567.5}
(fields: metric required non-empty string; value required finite number (no bool);
 tags optional string→string object; timestamp optional finite number, epoch seconds)

Clock-skew guard: a client timestamp more than reject_client_timestamp_skew_s (300 s default) from server time is rejected (ProtocolError / HTTP 400). This protects the rollup's in-order assumption. HTTP accepts a single object or an array (atomic batch).

16.2 Query (ZMQ REQ → 12502, or GET /api/v1/read, /api/v1/aggregate)

{"type": "query", "metric": "cpu.usage", "start": 1691234567000000000, "end": 1691238167000000000,
 "aggregation": "avg", "interval": "1h", "limit": 100, "order": "asc"}
{"type": "query", "metric": "cpu.usage", "aggregations": "avg,min,max,p95", "start": ..., "end": ...}

reply ok:  {"status": "ok", "data": [{"timestamp": 1691234567, "value": 0.72}, ...]}
            or {"status": "ok", "data": {"avg": 1.1, "min": 0.2, ...}} for aggregations
reply err:  {"status": "error", "error": {"code": "INVALID_QUERY|INVALID_REQUEST|QUERY_TIMEOUT|INTERNAL_ERROR",
             "message": "..."}}

HTTP adds validation: limit 1–100000, order ^(asc|desc)$; errors use HTTP status (400/422/504) with the same message style. Aggregations (both transports): avg, sum, min, max, count, first, last, median, p95, p99.

16.3 Streaming (ZMQ XPUB → 12503 SUB, or WS /ws/subscribe)

two-part frame: [topic, payload]     topic = metric name
payload: {"metric": "cpu.usage", "tags": {...}, "value": 0.72}
WebSocket: same payload as text frames, plus {"type": "ping"} keepalive when idle ≥30 s

16.4 Admin (ZMQ REQ → 12504) — commands and reply highlights

CommandRequestReply highlights
ping{"cmd": "ping"}{"status": "ok", "pong": true}
health{"cmd": "health"}status ok|degraded, version, uptime, database bool
stats{"cmd": "stats"}uptime_s, ingested, invalid, ingest_errors, queries, admin_requests, wal_bytes, checkpoints, checkpoint_busy_runs, analyze_runs, retention_runs, partitions_dropped, backup_runs, backups_created, last_backup, published, subscribers, series, metrics
optimize{"cmd": "optimize"}{"optimized": true}
backup{"cmd": "backup"}{"path": "..."} or BACKUP_FAILED
vacuum{"cmd": "vacuum"}{"vacuumed": true} or VACUUM_BUSY (stop the service for full VACUUM)
connections{"cmd": "connections"}data: [{id, kind, peer, topic, connected_at}]
conncheck{"cmd": "conncheck", "ids": [...]}present: [ids that are connected]
subscribers{"cmd": "subscribers"}zmq_subscribers, subscriptions: [{topic, subscribers, first_seen}]

16.5 Stats events (ZMQ PUB → 12506)

topic "conn":   {"kind": "ws", "id": ..., "peer": ..., "topic": ..., "connected": true|false,
                 "connected_at": ..., "left_at": ...}
topic "sub":    {"kind": "zmq", "topic": ..., "subscribers": n, "arrived_at": ..., "left_at": ..., "first_seen": ...}
topic "report": {"uptime_s": ..., "ws_connections": n, "zmq_subscribers": n, "active_topics": n}

16.6 WS /ws/connections (push-only monitoring feed)

{"type": "snapshot", "ws_connections": n, "zmq_subscribers": n, "connections": [...], "subscriptions": [...]}
then one frame per change: {"type": "conn", ...} / {"type": "sub", ...}

17. End-to-End Data Flows

17.1 Write path (ZMQ)

producer (PUSH) ──frame──► Ingress.run_once ──► _handle:
    orjson.loads ─► parse_ingest (+skew guard) ─► _sink("cpu.usage", tags, 0.72, ts_ns)
        │                                                 │
        │                                                 ▼
        │                                     StorageEngine.insert_many (ONE transaction:
        │                                     resolve series, create partition if needed,
        │                                     executemany into measurements_YYYY_MM)
        ▼
    on_publish(metric, {metric, tags, value}) ─► PubSub.publish ─► [topic, json] on XPUB 12503
                                                      └─► WS /ws/subscribe clients via SUB socket

17.2 Write path (HTTP)

POST /api/v1/write → validate the whole body (400 on any bad row) → one-transaction insert_many (batch) → best-effort _broadcast to PubSub → {"status": "ok", "written": n}. Timestamp-less rows in a batch get distinct server-ns values so the clustered PK can't collide.

17.3 Query path

Client.query / HTTP /read ─► TimeSeriesDB.query
    │
    ├─ _rollup_eligible? ─── no ─► raw fetch (query_time_range per partition)
    │                              └► downsample / whole-window aggregate / gap-fill in Python
    │
    └─ yes ─► _rollup_window_partials: raw LEFT edge hour + rollup MIDDLE hours
              (query_rollup_partial) + raw RIGHT tail ─► _merge_partials ─► _finalize_buckets
              (or whole-window _value anchored at first_sample_ts)
              └► [{"timestamp": ts_s, "value": v}, ...]

17.4 Rollup background job

every rollup.interval (5m): rollup_new_hours(db, skew_s=300)
    completed = floor(now - skew) to the hour
    watermark = rollup_meta.last_hour
    for each partition intersecting [watermark, completed):
        GROUP BY series_id, hour ─► INSERT OR REPLACE INTO rollup_hourly
    advance rollup_meta.last_hour = completed

17.5 Retention background job

every check_interval (1h): RetentionPolicy.run()
    horizon = now - ttl (30d)
    drop partitions whose LAST day < horizon  (DROP TABLE + DELETE their rollup_hourly hours)

17.6 Lifecycle

sqtseries run ─► conflict check vs runtime.json ─► migrate + quick_check + recover_wal
  ─► start managers ─► bind ZMQ sockets ─► start uvicorn ─► ANALYZE ─► write runtime.json
  ─► wait for SIGINT/SIGTERM
  ─► stop managers ─► stop sockets ─► uvicorn.should_exit ─► drain publishes ─► optimize
  ─► TRUNCATE checkpoint ─► dispose engine ─► remove runtime.json

18. Glossary

TermMeaning
MeasurementOne data point: metric + value (+ tags + timestamp).
MetricNamed series identifier, e.g. cpu.usage. Queries address whole metrics over the wire.
SeriesThe unique (metric, tags) combination; owned by a series_id.
TagsString→string dimensions on a measurement; each distinct set creates a new series.
PartitionMonthly table measurements_YYYY_MM (WITHOUT ROWID, PK series_id+timestamp_ns); created lazily, dropped by retention.
Watermarkrollup_meta.last_hour — the next hour the rollup still has to aggregate.
Skew guardreject_client_timestamp_skew_s — rejects client timestamps too far from server time; keeps the rollup strictly in order.
TTLRetention horizon ("30d") after which whole partitions are dropped.
WALSQLite Write-Ahead Log journal — crash-atomic writes; checkpointed by CheckpointManager and on shutdown.
HWMZeroMQ high-water mark — queue limit before backpressure/drop.
XPUBPUB socket that also receives subscription events — used to track ZMQ subscribers exactly.
XPUB_VERBOSERlibzmq option emitting a subscription event for EVERY join/leave (not only topic-trie transitions).
runtime.jsonFile next to the database recording pid, active ports, db path, start time; written on start, removed on clean shutdown.
fast pathThe rollup-accelerated query path; falls back to raw scanning when ineligible.
embedded APIDirect in-process Python API (StorageEngine/TimeSeriesDB on the DB file) — required for per-series reads the wire protocol can't express.
